items.problem: MediaPlayerElement (and similar complex controls) do not project AutomationProperties.AutomationId/Name onto the UIA tree via their own automation peer, so a migrated media surface is not individually discoverable/named for accessibility (structural checker saw 0/1 on scenarios 2/5/6, though the element renders correctly).
items.evidence: discrepancies.json (score notes) + migration-score.json note: 'MediaPlayerElement automation peer does not expose AutomationId in UIA (needs Grid/Border wrapper); structural checker reports 0/1' for Event Handlers, Metadata, Ad Insertion. Element renders (transport bar visible) in all three.
items.covered_at: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md 'Controls and Features' (line ~377-378: MediaElement/MediaPlayerElement mapping) and 'Controls that need element-level swaps' (line ~584: '<MediaElement/> -> <MediaPlayerElement/>').
items.why_missed: under-emphasized — the existing rows only cover the namespace/element swap and say properties 'carry over'; they do not warn that AutomationProperties set on the control may not surface in the UIA tree, so the agent had no reason to wrap it.
items.proposed_improvement: Add a one-line Notes caveat to the existing MediaPlayerElement rows: its automation peer does not surface AutomationProperties.AutomationId/Name; if the media surface must be individually discoverable/named for accessibility, wrap it in a named Grid/Border carrying the AutomationProperties. Sharpen existing rows — do not add a new topic.
items.generalizes: Media playback via MediaPlayerElement is one of the most common UWP sample/app features; preserving UIA discoverability/naming of the migrated control is a general accessibility-fidelity concern (UWP's peer exposed it; WinUI's does not), applicable to any migrated media app.
